Subject: PulseMed discovery recap + proposed POC success criteria

Hi Aisha — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our call and a short proposal for the POC so we can lock the kickoff date.

Call highlights
- Primary goal: reduce average time-to-insight for patient triage workflows using Redwood-hosted LLMs.
- Main constraints: PHI redaction pipeline in front of the model, strict latency SLAs for triage UI, and budget guardrails.

Proposed POC (2 weeks / lightweight evaluation) — please confirm these are reasonable:
1) Success metrics (measurable):
   - Latency: 95th percentile end-to-end inference latency < 300 ms (goal: < 200 ms)
   - Throughput: sustained throughput of 80 requests/sec on the demo workload (burst to 250 req/s)
   - Cost: target average model cost <= $0.002 per token for evaluation mix (we'll show tradeoffs for quantized variants)
   - Quality: >= 92% pass rate on your adjudication set (we'll take your sample prompts + 200 labeled examples)
2) Evaluation plan:
   - Baseline: run 3 representative customer flows (triage short, triage long, summary) against current system and Redwood variants
   - Dataset: you provide a 200-example labeled set + 1k anonymized prompts for throughput tests
   - Instrumentation: Redwood will produce per-token cost reports, latency histograms, and confusion breakdown by intent
3) Ownership & roles:
   - PulseMed: data owner & label adjudication (Aisha / Liam), security contact (security@pulse-med.com)
   - Redwood: Jordan (AE) — POC lead & kickoff; Ben (SRE/Benchmarks) — load tests and runbook; Marissa (CS) — onboarding and quality evaluation
4) Timeline / next steps:
   - Proposed kickoff: Mon Aug 16 (2 weeks) — target wrap: Fri Aug 27
   - Action: Aisha, please confirm dataset availability and preferred kickoff window; we’ll send a one-page POC checklist and a draft SLA for review.

Attached: pulsemed-poc-checklist.xlsx (high-level checklist and required inputs).

If the targets above look off, tell us which metric to relax and we’ll rework the tradeoffs (latency vs cost vs quality).

Thanks — Jordan
